To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the drug-particle interactions are influenced by the mode of particle preparation and the type of carrier system.
the mode of drug incorporation into the carrier matrix is the decisive factor for drug penetration into the stratum corneum.
the interaction between the drug and the carrier system is dependent on the concentration of drug molecules in the carrier system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel drug delivery systems for the topical treatment of skin diseases.
a better understanding of the interaction between drug molecules and nanoparticular carrier system.
the development of new carrier systems for the dermal administration of drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction of the drug molecules with the carrier system is a function of the drug concentration.
the drug-particle interaction is influenced by the drug concentration, the type of the carrier system and the mode of the drug incorporation into the particle.
in the case of SLN the drug molecule is located on the rim and in the case of NLC and the NE the drug is located in the matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the drug molecules are located in the vicinity of the carrier surface in case of SLN and NLC, but are located in the bulk in the case of NE.
drug molecules are incorporated into the carrier system by different mechanisms.
the mode of drug incorporation into the carrier systems influences the drug-particle interaction and thus the drug release from the carrier systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mode of drug loading into nanoparticulate carriers is crucial for drug release.
drug-particle interaction is a complex process which is influenced by the drug's molecular structure and the particle's physico-chemical properties.
drug penetration into the stratum corneum can be influenced by the mode of interaction of the drug with the carrier system.
